title: Active Related-Key Security of FAST
summary: FAST has proven multi-target security, but proving security when active related-key adversaries force relations between target keys remains open.

formal_statement.body: Prove FAST secure against active related-key attacks allowing a relation such as $K_2=K_1+1$.

scope.domain: Format-preserving encryption security for FAST under active related-key attacks.
assumptions: The PRF used by FAST resists related-key attacks.
parameters: K1 and K2: target keys whose relation may be forced, with K2 equal to K1 plus one as the example
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove FAST secure against active related-key attacks that permit forced relations between target keys.

citations.label: FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization

progress.summary: After proving multi-target security and discussing passive related-key attacks via a PRF assumption, the paper identifies active related-key security as a further direction. It says a related-key-resistant PRF would yield security, but does not prove the result for FAST.
citation_labels: F. Betül Durak et al., FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization
